Honda’s All-New Avancier SUV Rendered, Is This What It Will Look Like?
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
Do you remember the Honda Avancier ? Well, you probably do, because the original one was offered strictly as a station wagon, building on the era’s Accord and Odyssey, and it was a Japan-only model.
Production spanned between 1999 and 2003, taking place at the Sayama factory in Saitama, Japan, and this model was offered with a couple of powertrain options. The base one came with a straight-six that had a 2.3-liter displacement, and the superior one had a 3.0-liter V6. A four- and a five-speed automatic transmission, respectively, channeled the power to the wheels.
There was a 13-year hiatus between the original Honda Avancier and its successor, because the latter came out in 2016. And as you probably know, it is still around today. The model is also known as the Honda UR-V (Dongfeng Honda), and this one comes to life at Wuhan, in China, whereas the regular Avancier (GAC Honda) is made at Guangzhou.
This model is based on the Global Light Truck Platform 2, sharing its nuts and bolts with the third-generation Acura MDX. It has two gasoline engine options, which are mated either to a CVT (continuously variable transmission) or a nine-speed gearbox from ZF, depending on the configuration, and while the entry-level is front-wheel drive, the superior grade comes with all-wheel drive.
Honda’s current Avancier marketed in the People’s Republic is 189.6 inches (4,816 mm) long, 76.5 inches (1,942 mm) wide, and 65.7 inches (1,669 mm) tall. It has a 111-inch (2,820 mm) long wheelbase, and tips the scales at between under 3,800 and over 4,100 pounds (1.7-1.8+ metric tons). The Avancier was updated in 2020, getting modified front and rear fascias, and a few other things, and another mid-cycle refresh was performed three years later.
Photo: Kolesa Now, that same nameplate will be used for an entirely new high-rider. The upcoming Honda Avancier was recently teased, and it was the company’s Australian branch that dropped the official previews online. The short video has partially revealed the model from a few angles, and those teasers were used by Kolesa’ Nikita Chuyko to offer an unofficial yet quite realistic glimpse into the model that is right around the corner.
Care to discuss some of the design details? Well, up front, it features a closed-off grille, flanked by a pair of slim headlights that somewhat remind us of other models from different brands, such as the Range Rover Evoque. And they’re not the only things reminding us of the Evoque , because so do some of the hood’s styling cues.
On the sides, it features flush door handles, and the roofline is a bit arched toward the rear, ending with a pair of rather thick pillars, and a spoiler. There are more things at the rear that remind us of certain Range Rovers, like the lighting units, which mix a pair of vertical taillights with a thin light strip linking them together in the middle of the tailgate.
The Honda logo sits right below the light strip and above the Avancier emblem. The tailgate features a recess for the license plate, and seems to have a large opening. The rear bumper is quite short, and we can see a discreet diffuser attached to it.
This new design is expected to be seen on other vehicles from the Japanese company in the future, and here, we could mention the next generation Civic and the Accord, albeit with the necessary adjustments, and perhaps other modifications to easily tell these models apart.
Photo: Kolesa Word on the street is that the new-gen Honda Avancier will feature a three-row layout with seating for up to seven. Therefore, it should be more practical compared to the CR-V , and it should also be slightly larger. The cockpit will eventually open up to the camera, and we will be able to drop more lines about it when it does.
A new generation of the Honda self-charging hybrid assembly could power the next-gen Avancier, and some outlets believe that it could be based on a 2-liter four-cylinder engine, which should be updated, and details such as the output and thrust will be released in due course.
The second-gen Honda Avancier is expected to come to life in Prachinburi, Thailand, and from there, it will be exported to other countries. Australia will be on the list, and it looks like the model will also be sold in Japan, as well as perhaps other markets in the region.
It is yet unknown when the official unveiling of the new Honda Avancier will take place, but the model could be a few months away from revealing all of its secrets. When it will finally arrive at dealers, it will take on the likes of the Toyota Highlander, Kia Sorento, Mazda CX-80, and others. And before that happens, what’s your take on the design as previewed by the quoted outlet ? Do you fancy the looks?
